user.title: Grid purchase meter
user.description: Tarifwacht books your grid purchase per quarter hour under each tariff – the dynamic one with the price of exactly that quarter hour. The comparison assumes the same consumption pattern for every tariff.

data_description.name: For example “House”. Used in entity names.
data_description.meter_entity: Energy drawn from the grid (Wh, kWh or MWh, cumulative). Best: the meter at the grid connection point.

reconfigure.title: Grid purchase meter
reconfigure.description: Tarifwacht books your grid purchase per quarter hour under each tariff – the dynamic one with the price of exactly that quarter hour. The comparison assumes the same consumption pattern for every tariff.

data_description.name: For example “House”. Used in entity names.
data_description.meter_entity: Energy drawn from the grid (Wh, kWh or MWh, cumulative). Best: the meter at the grid connection point.

tariffs.title: Tariffs
tariffs.description: Enter all prices including VAT. For a fair comparison, both sides must contain the same price components (grid fees, levies, taxes). More tariffs can be added afterwards.

data.fixed_base: Fixed price: base price per month

data_description.fixed_price: Price per kWh from your contract or offer.
data_description.fixed_base: Optional. Booked pro rata per day.
data_description.dynamic_price_entity: A sensor with the total price per quarter hour in €/kWh (exchange price plus all surcharges, incl. VAT), ideally with a forecast attribute `data`, e.g. the total price of the EPEX Spot integration. This tariff calculates only from the setup on – to also look back, add it afterwards as “exchange price plus surcharges”.
data_description.dynamic_base: Optional. Booked pro rata per day.

user.title: Add tariff
user.description: Which kind of tariff? Tarifwacht computes every tariff over the whole period since setup.

menu_options.dynamic_total: Dynamic: sensor with the total price

fixed.title: Fixed price
fixed.description: Prices including VAT, as on your contract or offer.

data_description.name: For example the supplier. Used in entity names.
data_description.base_price: Optional. Booked pro rata per day.
data_description.current: The other tariffs show their difference to this one.

dynamic_total.title: Dynamic tariff: total price sensor
dynamic_total.description: A sensor that already contains the whole price per kWh: exchange price plus grid fee, levies, taxes, supplier surcharge and VAT. Calculates only from the setup on (no lookback, no import of statistics) – for that, choose “exchange price plus surcharges”.

data_description.name: For example the supplier. Used in entity names.
data_description.price_entity: In €/kWh, ideally with a price forecast per quarter hour or hour: the total price of the EPEX Spot integration, or (experimental) Nord Pool or ENTSO-E from HACS.
data_description.base_price: Optional, incl. VAT. Booked pro rata per day.
data_description.current: The other tariffs show their difference to this one.

dynamic_market.title: Dynamic tariff: exchange price plus surcharges
dynamic_market.description: Price per kWh = (exchange price + grid fee + taxes and levies + supplier surcharge) × (1 + VAT). Enter the surcharges net, as on the price sheets of supplier and grid operator.

data_description.name: For example the supplier. Used in entity names.
data_description.price_entity: Day-ahead price in €/kWh without VAT, ideally with a forecast: the market price of the EPEX Spot integration, or (experimental) Nord Pool or ENTSO-E from HACS, each without VAT and surcharges.
data_description.grid_fee: Energy-related grid fee of your grid operator, net.
data_description.levies: Electricity tax, concession fee and levies, net – as listed on the price sheet.
data_description.margin: What the supplier adds per kWh, net. With EPEX Spot: its absolute surcharge in cent (0.15 €/kWh = 15 ct); then leave grid fee and taxes empty.
data_description.base_price: Optional, incl. VAT. Booked pro rata per day.
data_description.current: The other tariffs show their difference to this one.

menu_options.edit: Edit tariff (name, current tariff, prices from the start)
menu_options.add_change: Add a price change from a date

add_change.title: Price change ({tariff})
add_change.description: From this date on (local midnight) the new prices apply; before it the previous ones stay. Prefilled with the prices valid today.

data.quarters: Quarters in which the windows apply

data_description.nt_windows: Local time, quarter-hour grid, several separated by commas, e.g. 10:00-14:00 or 01:45-06:15, 22:30-24:00. A window may run past midnight (23:00-06:00).
data_description.ht_windows: As above, e.g. 17:00-22:00. Outside all windows the standard grid fee applies.

remove_change.title: Remove a price change ({tariff})
remove_change.description: From then on the prices before that change apply again.

modul3.title: Modul 3 ({tariff})
modul3.description: With a controllable device (heat pump, wallbox) under § 14a EnWG Modul 3, the grid fee depends on the time of day: low-load (NT) and high-load (HT) windows, the standard grid fee of this tariff ({grid_fee} ct/kWh) at all other times. Applies to all grid purchase of the meter. Values from the start of the tariff; a new price sheet goes in as a price change.

data.quarters: Quarters in which the windows apply

data_description.nt: ct/kWh net, from your grid operator's price sheet (Modul 3).
data_description.ht: ct/kWh net, from your grid operator's price sheet (Modul 3).
data_description.quarters: Outside these quarters the standard grid fee applies all day.
data_description.nt_windows: Local time, quarter-hour grid, several separated by commas, e.g. 10:00-14:00 or 01:45-06:15, 22:30-24:00. A window may run past midnight (23:00-06:00).
data_description.ht_windows: As above, e.g. 17:00-22:00. Outside all windows the standard grid fee applies.

compare.name: Compare tariffs
compare.description: Cost of every tariff of a meter in a period, the cheapest first, also per month. Before the setup estimated from the hourly long-term statistics; Tarifwacht loads the exchange prices of that time from SMARD.de.

start.name: Start
start.description: Optional. Without: since the setup. An earlier start uses the meter's hourly values from the long-term statistics.

import_statistics.name: Import statistics
import_statistics.description: Writes the hours before the sensors' first long-term statistics (energy, costs, difference) so statistics cards and graphs also show the time before the setup. Changes the statistics database – create a backup first.

config_entry.name: Meter
config_entry.description: The Tarifwacht entry whose sensors get the history.

start.name: Start
start.description: First day to import, before the setup. Not earlier than the meter's long-term statistics.

start_after_end.message: The start must be before the end.

smard_failed.message: Exchange prices could not be loaded from SMARD.de ({error}). Please try again later.

import_start_after_setup.message: The start must be before the setup of this entry – after it, the sensors already have statistics.

import_no_statistics_yet.message: The sensors have no statistics yet. Home Assistant creates them every hour – please try again in an hour.

import_nothing_to_import.message: Nothing to import: the statistics already reach back to this day.

import_prices_missing.message: Nothing imported: every tariff lacks prices in this period. A tariff with a total price sensor has no prices from before the setup – add it as “exchange price plus surcharges” as well.

price_unit.title: Price sensor with an unsupported unit ({name})
price_unit.description: The price sensor {entity} reports {unit}. Tarifwacht uses prices as they are and needs €/kWh, so it ignores this sensor's prices for now. Set the unit to €/kWh in the price integration, or choose another sensor for the tariff (Tarifwacht → tariff → Reconfigure). This message disappears once the sensor reports €/kWh.

meter_unit.title: Meter with an unsupported unit ({name})
meter_unit.description: The meter {entity} reports {unit}. Tarifwacht needs Wh, kWh or MWh and books nothing until then. Choose another meter (Tarifwacht → ⋮ → Reconfigure). This message disappears once the meter reports a supported unit.

late_prices.title: Prices missing ({name})
late_prices.description: For {tariffs}, the price of a past quarter hour is still missing. Day-ahead prices are normally known the day before, so the price sensor may have failed. Consumption waits for its price for 24 hours; after that it is counted without a price (never as free). This message disappears once the prices arrive.

backfill_failed.title: Consumption could not be read from the recorder ({name})
backfill_failed.description: After the update from 0.1.0b1, Tarifwacht reads the consumption since setup from the recorder once. This failed: {error}. Live booking is not affected; the next start of Home Assistant tries again.
